Loan.title: Loan
Loan.description: Represents a single auto loan with its core parameters and administrative details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Loan entity.

userId.description: ID of the user who owns this loan. (Relationship: User 1:N Loan)

name.description: A user-defined name or reference for the loan, e.g., 'Car Loan - John Doe'.

principalAmount.description: The initial principal amount of the loan, in the specified currency.

annualInterestRate.description: The annual interest rate of the loan, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5.5 for 5.5%).

termInMonths.description: The total duration of the loan in months.

startDate.description: The start date of the loan.

currency.description: The currency in which the loan is denominated (e.g., 'AED', 'USD', 'EUR').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the loan record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the loan record was last updated.

AmortizationSchedulePeriod.title: AmortizationSchedulePeriod
AmortizationSchedulePeriod.description: Represents a single period within the loan's amortization schedule, calculated using the IFRS 9 EIR method.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AmortizationSchedulePeriod entity.

loanId.description: Reference to the parent Loan entity. (Relationship: Loan 1:N AmortizationSchedulePeriod)

periodNumber.description: The sequential number of the amortization period, starting from 1.

date.description: The end date of the amortization period.

openingBalance.description: The outstanding principal balance at the beginning of the period.

interestAccrual.description: The amount of interest accrued during this period based on the opening balance and monthly effective interest rate.

principalPortion.description: The portion of the total payment that reduces the principal balance.

totalPayment.description: The total payment made or due for this period (sum of principal portion and interest accrual).

closingBalance.description: The outstanding principal balance at the end of the period.

cumulativeInterest.description: The total interest accrued from the start of the loan up to the end of this period.

status.description: The current status of the amortization period (e.g., 'projected', 'paid', 'recalculated').

AuditEntry.title: AuditEntry
AuditEntry.description: Records every significant user action or system event related to a loan, forming an immutable audit trail.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AuditEntry entity.

loanId.description: Reference to the parent Loan entity for which the action was performed. (Relationship: Loan 1:N AuditEntry)

userId.description: ID of the user who performed the action. (Relationship: User 1:N AuditEntry)

timestamp.description: The date and time when the action was logged.

actionType.description: The category of action performed (e.g., 'Schedule Generated', 'Interest Rate Change', 'Period Marked Paid', 'Export Excel').

description.description: A detailed, human-readable description of the action that occurred.

oldValue.description: The value or state of relevant data before the action, typically stored as a stringified representation (e.g., old interest rate, old status).

newValue.description: The value or state of relevant data after the action, typically stored as a stringified representation (e.g., new interest rate, new status).

reason.description: Optional: A user-provided reason or justification for certain actions, such as an interest rate change.

JournalEntryLine.title: JournalEntryLine
JournalEntryLine.description: Represents a single line item of a double-entry journal entry generated for a loan period, compatible with Odoo ERP.

id.description: Unique identifier for the JournalEntryLine entity.

loanId.description: Reference to the parent Loan entity for which this journal entry line was generated. (Relationship: Loan 1:N JournalEntryLine)

periodNumber.description: The amortization period number to which this journal entry line pertains. (Relationship: AmortizationSchedulePeriod 1:N JournalEntryLine)

entryType.description: The logical type of journal entry this line belongs to (e.g., 'Accrual Entry', 'Payment Entry').

journal.description: The name or code of the accounting journal where this entry is recorded (e.g., 'General Ledger').

date.description: The date of the journal entry line.

reference.description: A descriptive reference text for the journal entry line, e.g., 'Loan Amortization Period X Accrual'.

accountCode.description: The general ledger account code affected by this entry (e.g., '6110 Interest Expense').

accountName.description: The descriptive name of the account (e.g., 'Interest Expense').

debit.description: The debit amount for this journal entry line. Will be 0 if the entry is a credit.

credit.description: The credit amount for this journal entry line. Will be 0 if the entry is a debit.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to adhere strictly to the core design principles, prioritizing Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC, and QAPs. The primary design choice places each user's loans in a top-level collection `loans/{loanId}`, where the `Loan` document itself contains the `userId`. This directly supports the requirement for users to only access their own loans.

**Authorization Independence (Critical Denormalization):**
To achieve Authorization Independence and avoid costly, complex `get()` calls in Firestore Security Rules, the `userId` of the parent `Loan` document will be denormalized and copied into every document within its subcollections: `schedule` (AmortizationSchedulePeriod) and `journalEntries` (JournalEntryLine). The `auditTrail` (AuditEntry) entity already includes `userId`, making it inherently authorization-independent. This strategy ensures that security rules for any document (Loan, Schedule Period, Journal Entry, Audit Entry) can be evaluated atomically by simply checking `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId`, without needing to read parent documents. This is crucial for robust security, simplifies debugging, and enables atomic batch writes (e.g., creating a loan and its entire schedule).

**QAPs (Queryable Access Patterns):**
This structure directly supports efficient and secure Queryable Access Patterns (QAPs). For the `loans` collection, a user can query `db.collection('loans').where('userId', '==', auth.currentUser.uid)` to retrieve only their own loans. Similarly, for subcollections like `schedule`, the denormalized `userId` allows for direct security rules (`allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId;`). While application code would typically filter subcollections by the `loanId` (e.g., `db.collection('loans').doc(loanId).collection('schedule')`), the underlying security rule relies on the `userId` within *each* schedule document, ensuring that even if `loanId` were somehow compromised, the `userId` check would still enforce correct ownership. This eliminates the need for rules to `get()` the parent `loan` document to verify `userId`, thus supporting secure `list` operations without relying on rules as filters. Each collection maintains a homogeneous security posture (user-owned data), further simplifying rules and ensuring predictable access patterns.
